note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 143, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: The named army elements are the source forces for the full Ligny date, not an attempt to quantify the entire Prussian or French national army. No additional political identity is guessed.

The National Army Museum identifies the French and Prussian armies at Ligny and the separate French force at Quatre Bras in the 1815 campaign. The named CDB90 force receives an explicit representative shako-and-musket infantry component; this is not an exact regimental uniform, a classification of every soldier, or a reconstruction of cavalry/artillery shares. At Quatre Bras the British-Dutch aggregate retains its own identity and receives no new equipment assignment. All CDB90 quantities and side labels are preserved.
